name: Tali Harris
life: “I still remember working a full evening with pay promised in samples.” Friday often includes a stop at the bank steps, where Tali takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I own the salon. I used to complain about my own boss doing exactly this, which the oldest technician remembers.
appearance: Tali is easy to recognize by a smooth side part with one rebellious curl and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip, Tali draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first when listening.
personality: Tali talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Tali's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To get the offer into terms the old shop self would have accepted.
family: Ana Crane is Tali’s second cousin. Tali remembers the birthdays. Ana asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The understudy sings*, Ana says, “I am the parent's friend who wanted a benefit concert.”
connections: Aldo Dixon (salon worker). The worker who would quit explains the exact terms the owner once protested herself.

reactions.situation: An apprentice asks if declining will cost future shifts
reactions.response: Tali asks the owner to give the apprentice a direct answer in front of a witness of their choosing.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Tali asks which apartment is expecting someone home and makes sure that household knows about the delay.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Tali says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
